response.sql: SELECT AVG(rebrate / feerate) AS avg_rebate_to_fee_ratio, COUNT(*) AS fee_record_count FROM fees WHERE feerate >= 0.0009;

assumptions.assumption: The population is every fees row with feerate >= 0.0009, including rows where rebrate is NULL. The count therefore includes those rows, while AVG skips them because a NULL ratio is ignored. Division is safe because feerate >= 0.0009 excludes zero.

alternatives.interpretation: Count only the fee records that contribute to the average, meaning those with a non-null rebrate as well as a qualifying feerate.
alternatives.sql: SELECT AVG(rebrate / feerate) AS avg_rebate_to_fee_ratio, COUNT(*) AS fee_record_count FROM fees WHERE feerate >= 0.0009 AND rebrate IS NOT NULL;
